title: CloudSensors
description: Which AWS-native sources and Vulnetix passes are read, for one account or for every account. The sources listed are turned on; every other source is turned off for that scope. Once a source is on, everything it reports is ingested: granularity stops at the source. Turning one off stops reading it and keeps the findings already ingested, with their triage history. Each source's consent record is a named inline policy on the execution role, attached by redeploying the stack, so set deploy to attach it in the same apply. Turning a source on needs a connected AWS account. Not stored yet for one account: CloudNativeSource.accountId exists and is keyed, but no route writes an account id and the stack deploy reads the sources for the whole tenant, so only account "*" applies today. A document naming an account validates, and applying it needs that write path and a per-account read in the deploy.

account.description: An AWS account id, or * for every account, including those connected later. One document per value.

sources.description: inspector: Amazon Inspector. security-hub: AWS Security Hub. guardduty, config, macie and access-analyzer: those products, read through Security Hub (one grant, filtered by product). waf: the AWS WAF configuration in front of the account. compute: SSM package inventory, EMR, EKS node groups, running ECS images, CIS AWS Foundations and CloudFormation template checks. compute-artifacts: read inside ECR image layers and Lambda code. network-logs: match Resolver and flow logs against malicious indicators. eks-workloads: list EKS pods and the images each runs; each cluster also needs an access entry you create. compute-artifacts, network-logs and eks-workloads have an effect only with compute on.

deploy.description: Redeploy the pipeline stack after a change, so the execution role carries exactly the policies the sources turned on need.
